Read this first

One brand system, localised by market

Pyle has one brand: the same red, the same rings, the same voice and the same promise wherever we sell. What changes from market to market is the regulatory layer: how we show prices, which languages we print, which conformity marks go on the box, and how we ask for permission to market to people.

Sections 1 and 2 are global and fixed. Sections 3 and 4 are regional and mandatory. Where a regional rule conflicts with a global brand rule, the regional rule wins. We then solve the brand problem inside the law, never around it.

Brand is the constant. Compliance is the local dialect.

Source of truth

Pyle USA — Visual Brand Identity Refresh (Jan 2025). Only the “Visual Brand New” direction applies. “Visual Brand Now” and “The Packaging Now” are deprecated and must not be reproduced.

Labels used in this guide

  • 48HD standard A rule 48HourDigital set where the source deck shows the asset but gives no numeric rule.
  • Sampled A value measured from the source artwork. Confirm it against the master files before print.
  • Regional A legal or regulatory requirement. Counsel confirms it before launch.

Mission & Vision

We turn up for you, so you turn nothing down.

Mission

Pyle exists to shorten the distance between something you’re thinking about and something you actually do. For more than 45 years we’ve made sound and hobbies accessible, so anyone with a spark of curiosity can plug in, start playing and feel it at full volume.

Vision

To be the world’s most welcoming way into sound. We want to be the first brand a beginner trusts, the go-to brand for the tinkerer, and the gift that turns someone else’s “maybe one day” into “today”, in every home, garage, boat, stage and backyard in every market we serve.

45+

years powering passions, hobbies and side projects

10

product categories: Automotive, Home, Instruments, Live Audio, Marine, Power, Production, Security, Tools & Accessories, Video

5

markets: USA, Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, Australia

The 45-year heritage story

Becoming downright unsilenceable.

For more than 45 years, Pyle has powered passions, hobbies, side projects and inspired gifts into existence. We built our name by making functional gear more accessible to hobbyists, newcomers, garage artists, analog DIYers and people building second setups.

Our promise has never changed. We lower the entry barriers so you can start at any budget, plug into anything easily, and feel it all at full output. We give you the luxury of tuning in, living out loud and feeling your dreams at full volume, until you become downright unsilenceable.

Now that promise is going international. From Toronto to Toulouse, Manchester to Melbourne, Pyle is bringing the same invitation to a new generation of makers, players and listeners.

“We have a half-century heritage of making functional gear more accessible. With lower entry barriers, you can get started at any budget, easily plug into anything, and feel it all at full output.”

Brand Archetype

80% Explorer. 20% Jester. 100% Pyle.

Pyle’s personality blends two archetypes in a fixed ratio. The Explorer leads: it gives every message its purpose. The Jester follows: it gives every message its spark. Get the ratio wrong and we sound either like a spec sheet or like a joke. Get it right and we sound like the friend who talks you into the thing you’ll love.

80%
Explorer

Explorer brands help you discover the world. Their products free your individuality, initiative and excitement, and turn experiences into growth.

Personality Matrix · Actionable tone rules

Eight traits, put to work.

TraitWe sound like…In practice
● Encouraging (Explorer)A friend who says “you’ve got this.”Lead with what the customer can do, not what the product is. “Start your first podcast tonight.”
● Confident (Explorer)Someone who’s done this for 45 years.State facts plainly. No hedging, no hype. “100 W peak. Bluetooth 5.0. Done.”
● Relatable (Explorer)A fellow hobbyist, not a salesperson.Use everyday words. Explain jargon the first time it appears.
● Experienced (Explorer)A trusted guide.Give one useful tip per touchpoint. Max Volume delivers it.
● Optimistic (Jester)Someone who sees the fun first.Frame upgrades and first purchases as beginnings, not risks.
● Laidback (Jester)Relaxed, never pushy.No false urgency, countdown pressure or fear-based selling.
● Nudging (Jester)A playful push off the fence.Short, active invitations: “Plug in. Turn up. Get into it!”
● Irreverent (Jester)A wink, not a sneer.Light wordplay and sound puns, at most one per piece. Never at the customer’s expense.
The 80/20 rule in copy: In any piece of copy, roughly four sentences inform, guide or inspire (Explorer) for every one that delights (Jester). Headlines may lean Jester. Specs, safety, legal and support copy are always 100% Explorer, with zero jokes.

Tone of Voice & Copywriting

Talk like a friend who knows gear.

EncouragingClearPlayfulHonest

Core copy principles

  1. Lead with the passion, then prove it. Open with what the customer gets to do, then back it up with the spec.
  2. Short beats long. Headlines: 2–6 words. Bullets: one benefit and one proof each. Sentences: under 20 words.
  3. Active, second person. “You”, “your”, “let’s”. Avoid “users” and “consumers”.
  4. Numbers are proof. Use real, verified figures: watts (state RMS or peak), frequency response, battery hours, IP rating.
  5. One wink per piece. One pun or playful line per asset, at most. Never in safety, legal or support copy.
  6. Truth is non-negotiable. Every claim must be substantiated, region-correct and approved (see Section 3).

Product listing formula

Title: Pyle [Product Name] — [Key Spec], [Key Feature], [Use Case]

Example: “Pyle 3.5" 2-Way Indoor/Outdoor Speaker System — IP67 Waterproof, 70–21 kHz, Universal Wall Mount”

  • Hook line: one sentence on the passion it unlocks.
  • 3–5 bullets: BENEFIT IN CAPS: proof in plain language.
  • What’s in the box · Tech specs table · Compatibility
  • Warranty & guarantee statement: region-specific (see Section 3).

Proof beats promises.

DoDon’t
“Weatherproof to IP67, so the party keeps going when the sky doesn’t cooperate.”“Totally waterproof! Use it anywhere!” (overclaims; IP67 has defined limits)

“Pairs with Bluetooth 5.0 phones, tablets and laptops.”“Works with everything.”
“Setup takes about 5 minutes. A step-by-step guide is in the box.”“Easy setup!” with no proof
“Designed in the USA” (badge, used exactly as supplied)“Made in the USA”, “American-made”, or editing the badge wording
Spell out units at first use: “Hz (hertz)” in beginner-facing copyStacking unexplained acronyms in a single bullet
Region-correct spelling, units, currency and guarantee wordingCopy-pasting US listings into CA, EU, UK or AU storefronts

Logo System

One wordmark. Three ways to wear it.

The refreshed PYLE wordmark keeps the heritage letterforms and sharpens them for screens, packaging and product. It is built on a precise construction grid and judged against five principles: Simplicity, Memorability, Timelessness, Versatility and Relevance.

1 · Primary Wordmark: PYLE

The default on every touchpoint: packaging fronts, web headers, advertising, social and documents.

2 · Stacked Icon: PY / LE

For small square formats: app icons, favicons, avatars, product badges, embossing, hang-tags. It never replaces the wordmark on pack fronts or in headlines.

3 · Vertical Lockup

For tall, narrow surfaces: speaker grille badges, tower speakers, mic stands, side gussets, tape. Reads top to bottom.

Logo · Approved colourways

Four approved backgrounds. No exceptions.

Hero · Red on Cream
Hero dark · Red on Maroon
Mono · Black on light
Mono · White on black

On photography

Use Cream or Accent Yellow on photography only where the logo area passes contrast (see the Colour contrast slide). Keep a calm, low-detail zone behind the mark.

Registered symbol ®

Use ® only in jurisdictions where the PYLE mark is registered. Where registration is pending or not held, use ™ or no symbol. Falsely claiming registration is an offence in several of our markets (including the UK and Australia). Brand Legal holds the master registration list.

48 HOUR DIGITAL | Brooklyn, NY | 347-817-1990Pyle Brand & Regional Style Guide v1.0 ·
Clearspace & minimum size 48HD standard

Give it room to be loud.

1X 1X 1X 1X
  • X = the cap height of the “P” in the wordmark as used.
  • Primary wordmark: 1X on all sides. Stacked icon: 0.5X. Vertical lockup: 0.5X left and right, 1X top and bottom.
  • No text, graphics, edges, folds or rings may enter the clearspace. Rings may run behind the logo only on full-bleed brand backgrounds where the logo passes contrast.
AssetPrintDigital
Primary wordmark20 mm wide80 px wide
Stacked icon10 mm wide32 px wide
16 px favicon uses a simplified, pixel-hinted file
Vertical lockup8 mm wide24 px wide
“Designed in the USA” badge12 mm diameter48 px diameter

Logo misuse: never

  • Stretch, condense, skew, outline or add effects (shadow, glow, bevel, gradient).
  • Recolour outside the approved colourways, or retype the logo in Parafina or any typeface.
  • Use the deprecated “Visual Brand Now” logo or the pre-refresh “PYLE® Experience Life!” lock-up.
  • Place it on busy photography without a contrast-safe zone.
  • Combine it with a sub-brand, retailer logo or tagline inside its clearspace.
  • Rotate the horizontal wordmark 90° to imitate the vertical lockup.

“Designed in the USA” badge

An endorsement, never a headline.

Left: dark outline on light or kraft backgrounds. Right: white on Pyle Red.

Placement

  • Packaging: Trust panel and lower-right of the Product panel.
  • Product pages: next to warranty and guarantee information.
  • Advertising: as an endorsement, never as the headline.

Rules

  • Never change the wording to “Made in”, “Built in” or “Engineered in”.
  • Never use the badge on a product that was not genuinely designed by Pyle’s US team.
  • Always show the true country of manufacture elsewhere on the pack (e.g., “Made in China”).
  • Never place the badge directly beside the country-of-origin line where the two could be read as one claim.
Canada · mandatory

Packaging sold in Canada carries the French badge, “CONÇU AUX ÉTATS-UNIS”, either as a bilingual roundel or paired with the English version at equal or greater prominence (see Regional · Canada).

Other languages · optional

EU language variants of the badge are optional. Translated badges are produced only from the master file by 48HourDigital.

Licensing

Manrope and Delicious Handrawn are open-licence (Google Fonts) families. Parafina is a commercial typeface. Confirm desktop, web, app and packaging seats before regional rollout.

Graphic System

The Pulse of Play

The heartbeat of Pyle.

“Pulse of Play” is our visual design system. It captures the dynamic essence of Pyle’s audio experience in concentric soundwave rings that radiate outward like sound from a speaker cone or the grooves of a record.

It stands for innovation, quality and the joy of sound that echoes through every product we create. With Pulse of Play, every beat and note is not just heard, but truly felt, across every visual touchpoint.

Radiating sound into every space.

48 HOUR DIGITAL | Brooklyn, NY | 347-817-1990Pyle Brand & Regional Style Guide v1.0 ·
Pulse of Play · Construction rules

Concentric. Even. Always from a source.

Red on Maroon · hero
Yellow on Cream · playful
Black on Kraft · carton
Deep Maroon on White
  • Rings are concentric and evenly spaced. Stroke weight and gap are equal (1 : 1) by default. A 1 : 1.5 gap is permitted on large formats.
  • The ring centre (the “source”) sits on a meaningful point: the product’s driver, a performer’s mouth or microphone, the logo, or deliberately off-canvas so arcs sweep in from a corner.
  • With photography: rings may wrap around or emerge from behind a cut-out subject to create depth. They never cross a face or obscure the product.
  • Motion: rings pulse outward from the source at tempo. Use 1–2 seconds per cycle, ease-out, and loop seamlessly. Respect prefers-reduced-motion with a static frame.
  • Never: distort rings into ellipses (except for perspective on 3D packshots), add gradients, mix more than two ring colours, or use rings as a text background below 7 : 1 contrast.

Brand Mascot

Meet Max Volume

Max is our Megaphone Mascot, a character who embodies the spirit of Pyle’s audio innovation and community engagement. Max is the voice of the brand. He delivers helpful tooltips, inspiring quotes and engaging content directly to our audience.

Where Max appears

  • Tooltips and “Tip:” call-outs in user guides, quick-start cards and product pages
  • Onboarding moments, empty states and success messages in digital products
  • Social content, packaging inserts, and community or event content

Max’s voice

Short, upbeat, useful. Always one actionable idea. Written in Delicious Handrawn inside a Cream speech bubble.

Don’t just listen — feel the sound! Try this feature for a sound that’s as big as life! Tip: Boost your bass by adjusting the EQ settings!
48 HOUR DIGITAL | Brooklyn, NY | 347-817-1990Pyle Brand & Regional Style Guide v1.0 ·
Max Volume · Usage rules
  1. Max appears once per layout, maximum.
  2. Max always speaks toward the content he refers to. The megaphone points at the bubble or the feature.
  3. Maintain 0.5× Max’s height in clearspace around the character and bubble.
  4. Minimum size: 24 mm / 64 px tall.
  5. Never recolour Max, change his expression set, add accessories, crop his face, or animate him off-model. All poses come from the master character sheet.
  6. Max is not used next to the “Designed in the USA” badge or regulatory marks.
  7. Localisation: Max’s lines are transcreated, not translated word for word. In Canada, every Max bubble on packaging and in Quebec-facing digital content must have a French version.

Max never delivers

Prices or promotions · safety warnings · legal or compliance statements · warranty or guarantee terms · apologies or complaint responses. Those are always plain Manrope copy.

48 HOUR DIGITAL | Brooklyn, NY | 347-817-1990Pyle Brand & Regional Style Guide v1.0 ·
Photography

Show the gear. Show the feeling.

A · E-commerce packshots

“The Proof”

  • Pure white background (#FFFFFF) for marketplace hero images; Light Grey or Cream for brand-site secondary images.
  • Product fills 85% of the frame, shot square (1:1), minimum 2000 × 2000 px.
  • Even, soft, shadowless or soft-contact-shadow lighting, with true-to-product colour.
  • Image set per SKU: hero 3/4 · front · back/inputs · scale-in-hand or in-context · what’s in the box · infographic (3 features, Manrope, max. 6 words each) · dimensions (dual units where required) · lifestyle.
  • No added logos, badges, watermarks, Max Volume or promotional text on hero images.
  • Regional accuracy: plugs, chargers and on-screen languages match the market: Type A/B (US/CA), C/F (EU), G (UK), I (AU). Never show a charger in markets where the product ships without one.
B · Lifestyle

“The Feeling”

  • Real people mid-passion: singing, playing, building, celebrating. Faces show joy, focus or surprise.
  • Warm natural light, lived-in environments, honest textures. No sterile studio sets.
  • Product is visible and in use. The scene is the hero, the gear is the enabler.
  • Pulse of Play rings may be composited to radiate from the product.
  • Casting reflects the diversity of each market, with a range of ages, abilities, body types and backgrounds, and matches our four personas.
  • PRO line: dark, high-contrast, coloured gels (cyan/red), performer close-ups. VINTAGE line: light grey sets, retro wardrobe, chrome and classic microphones.

Photography · Category direction
CategoryScene direction
HomeLiving rooms, bedrooms, home studios. Guitar on the sofa, piano corner, vinyl and retro radio. Warm, golden-hour interiors.
MarineBoats on bright water, docks, wakeboarding, harbour skylines. Saturated blues and teals, sun flare and spray. Gear shown weather-exposed but secure.

ProductionPodcast desks, streamers, bedroom producers. Mic close-ups, RGB accents kept subtle, shallow depth of field.

Outdoor & DigitalBillboards, transit, social. Bold Pyle Red frames with lifestyle crops and a single headline.

Never

  • Stock-looking, over-posed imagery.
  • AI-generated people presented as real customers.
  • Images that misrepresent size, finish or included accessories.
  • Unsafe use (unsecured marine installs, distracted driving).
  • Politicians, public figures, political rallies or protests, even organic or press photos of Pyle products in use. They imply endorsement, raise publicity-rights issues, and press images are licensed only for editorial use.

Packaging Standard · The 5-Pillar Panel System

Every box tells the whole story in five panels.

Every Pyle pack, from kraft master carton to full-colour retail box, is organised into five content pillars. Customers find the same information in the same place on every product, in every market.

1

Brand

Top panel & lead face. Instant recognition from any shelf angle.

Primary wordmark (largest element), Pulse of Play arcs, pyleusa.com. The top flap repeats the wordmark inverted so it reads when the box is opened.

2

Lifestyle

The emotional face. Show the feeling and the “why”.

Lifestyle photograph (consumer pack) or “The next thing you’ll love.” (master carton), with Pulse of Play composited around the product in use.

3

Product

Principal display panel. What it is and why it’s great, in 5 seconds.

Model number pill (e.g., PDWR35BK) · product name in Parafina · line art or photo · three key features in the yellow callout box · “Get Into It!” · USA badge · PRO/VINTAGE badge.

4

Technical

Side or back panel. Everything for the tinkerer.

Feature list with Product Feature Iconography, full specs table, I/O diagram, what’s in the box, compatibility, dimensions & weight (units by region). Order: Product → Feature → Spec → Benefit.

5

Trust

Base of technical panel / bottom. Safe, legal, accountable.

Barcode (UPC/EAN), country of manufacture, regulatory marks, warnings (e.g., Prop 65 in US), manufacturer & importer addresses, warranty/guarantee, recycling marks, support contact.

The Trust panel is the regional module. It is designed as a swappable “compliance strip”, so one master artwork can be released as US, CA, EU, UK and AU variants (see Section 3).

Packaging · Two pack tiers

Primary Master Carton

Natural kraft, one-colour black print. Pulse of Play arcs, line-art product, the same five-pillar logic. Sustainable, low ink, shipping-ready.

Primary Consumer

Full-colour Maroon pack (or the White variant for clean retail and e-commerce), lifestyle photo window, Accent Yellow feature box. Branded Pyle Red tape for direct-to-consumer shipments.

Packaging rules

  • The wordmark appears on at least four faces.
  • Feature callouts: maximum three on the front. Everything else goes to Technical.
  • No price, retailer-specific or time-limited claims are printed on pack.
  • All regulated text is in Manrope, black or white, at legal minimum size or larger.
  • Language-of-pack rules, regulatory marks and addresses vary by market. Follow Section 3 exactly.

Tell us using the form in your account or email [support address], then return the item within 14 days. We’ll refund the price and standard delivery within 14 days of getting it back. Mandatory text · use word for word on every warrantyOur goods come with guarantees that cannot be excluded under the Australian Consumer Law. Governance & review

Keeping the brand loud and the compliance tight.

01

Ownership

Brand owner: Pyle USA Marketing.
Guide custodian: 48HourDigital.

02

Approvals

Every new regional SKU pack, storefront and campaign is signed off by (1) Brand, (2) Regional Compliance or counsel, and (3) Localisation (native-speaker transcreation review for FR-CA, FR, DE and other EU languages).

03

Review cycle

Reviewed every six months, and immediately after any material regulatory change in a served market. Regional slides record the date they were last verified.

04

Asset source

Logos, the Max Volume character sheet, Pulse of Play pattern files, colour libraries (ASE / Pantone) and packaging dielines come only from the Pyle master brand library. Never rebuild them from screenshots.
